# GMEOW — Global Metadata and Entity Ontology for the Web documentation index

A reasoning-centric, OWL 2 DL, upper-ontology-grounded super-vocabulary that unifies document metadata, entity descriptions, legal agreements, contacts and person-centric data. GMEOW is grounded in gUFO and aligned to FOAF, REL, DOAP, PROV-O, schema.org and Wikidata.

## Recipes
- person-names-and-display: Model Person Names Without a Preferred-Name Slot; terms gmeow:Person, gmeow:PersonName, gmeow:NameUsage, gmeow:displayable
- contested-or-attributed-facts: Model Contested or Attributed Facts; terms gmeow:StandpointClaim, gmeow:vantage, gmeow:claimModality, gmeow:accordingTo
- events-and-participants: Model Events and Participants; terms gmeow:Event, gmeow:Participation, gmeow:TimeInterval, gmeow:Place
- documents-and-schema-org: Publish Documents for Schema.org Consumers; terms gmeow:Document, gmeow:webUrl, gmeow:Entity
- offline-gts-distribution: Describe Offline GTS Distribution; terms gmeow:GTSDocument, gmeow:GTSProfile, gmeow:GTSSegment
- graph-rag-dataset-lineage: Model Graph-RAG Dataset Lineage; terms gmeow:Dataset, gmeow:Chunk, gmeow:ExtractedEntity, gmeow:EvidenceSpan

- gmeow:AccountStatus (class; gmeow:slices/accounts): The usage status of an account from its holder's standpoint — a VALUE vocabulary (active, dormant, historical, …); open set.
- gmeow:AcquaintanceRelationship (class; gmeow:slices/contacts): An interpersonal relationship of social acquaintance — agents who have met and know one another (the reified form of hasMet).

- gmeow:accountBalance (property; gmeow:slices/finance): The current balance of a financial account, expressed as a MonetaryAmount. Non-functional: a multi-currency account has several balances, and competing standpoint-indexed balance claims coexist (Principle 9).
- gmeow:accountCurrency (property; gmeow:slices/finance): The currency(ies) of a financial account, drawn from the open currency reference-frame vocabulary (gmeow:frameRealmCurrency). NON-FUNCTIONAL: a single account may hold balances in several currencies (multi-currency fintech accounts).
- gmeow:accountHolder (property; gmeow:slices/finance): Relates a financial account to the agent that holds it. Non-functional: a joint account has several co-equal holders.
- gmeow:accountKey (property; gmeow:slices/trust): Relates an online account to the cryptographic key that identifies it — the seam joining a decentralized-identity account (e.g. a Nostr account's nostrPubkey literal) to the key as a first-class entity.
- gmeow:accountName (property; gmeow:slices/accounts): The handle or user name identifying the account on its service.
- gmeow:accountNumber (property; gmeow:slices/finance): The account number identifying the financial account at its institution. Not functional: different sources may report differing formats.
- gmeow:accountService (property; gmeow:slices/accounts): The online service an account is held with. Functional — an account is on one service.
- gmeow:accountServiceHomepage (property; gmeow:slices/accounts): The homepage of the service an account is held with — the foaf:accountServiceHomepage of FOAF's OnlineAccount idiom. Range open (an IRI).
- gmeow:accountStatus (property; gmeow:slices/accounts): The holder's usage status of an account — a gmeow:AccountStatus value (active / dormant / historical). A retired account is status 'historical' with validUntil in the past, never deleted (P10).
- gmeow:accountType (property; gmeow:slices/finance): The kind of financial account — one of the open gmeow:FinancialAccountType values (bank, credit, investment, wallet). Functional: an account has one canonical type; several types are several accounts.

- gmeow:addressPlace (property; gmeow:slices/contacts): The geographic place a postal address denotes (typically the premises/building) — the seam from the as-written address to the resolved place hierarchy, its coordinates/geometry, and its external identifiers.

- gmeow:celestialEpoch (property; gmeow:slices/places): The epoch (Julian year, e.g. 2000.0) for which the coordinates are expressed. Required for proper-motion propagation; frame-relative per Principle 11.
- gmeow:celestialObjectType (property; gmeow:slices/places): The kind(s) of a celestial location (one or more gmeow:CelestialObjectType individuals). Non-functional: multi-source classifications may differ (e.g. a source classified as both 'star' and 'variable star') and must coexist as evidence.
- gmeow:centsFromOrigin (property; gmeow:slices/music): A convenience measure of a pitch or interval in cents, generated from the exact ratio by fnRatioToCents. Not canonical; the ratio pair is canonical (Principle 4).
- gmeow:certificationLevel (property; gmeow:slices/trust): How carefully the binding was verified (OpenPGP certification level): generic, persona, casual, or positive.
- gmeow:certifiedIdentity (property; gmeow:slices/trust): The agent identity a certification binds the key to.
- gmeow:certifiedKey (property; gmeow:slices/trust): The cryptographic key a certification vouches for.
- gmeow:certifier (property; gmeow:slices/trust): The agent that made a certification.
- gmeow:chainId (property; gmeow:slices/attestation): The chain identifier of a blockchain network (e.g. CAIP-2 chainId, eip155:1).
- gmeow:changeType (property; gmeow:slices/languages): The kind(s) of linguistic change occurring — sound shift, borrowing, standardization, extinction, etc. NON-FUNCTIONAL: a single event may instantiate multiple change types from different analytical standpoints.
- gmeow:charset (property; gmeow:slices/email): The character encoding of a MIME part's content (e.g. utf-8, iso-8859-1). Stored as a literal because the IANA charset registry is too open to enumerate as a closed value vocabulary.

- gmeow:chunkOf (property; gmeow:slices/ai): The source information object this chunk segments. Functional: a chunk is cut from exactly one source; re-chunking produces new Chunk individuals, never a re-pointed one.

- gmeow:cites (property; gmeow:slices/citations): Relates an entity to a creative work it cites — the flat 80%-case shortcut. Non-functional: an entity may cite many works. Promote to a gmeow:CitationAct node when the intent, selector, provenance, or standpoint of the citation must be rec...
- gmeow:citingEntity (property; gmeow:slices/citations): The entity that makes the citation — a claim, a work, a module, a dataset. Functional per relator: one citing entity per CitationAct.

- gmeow:cloneUrl (property; gmeow:slices/software): A URL from which the repository can be cloned. Non-functional: multiple protocols (https, ssh, git) may be available.
- gmeow:closesAt (property; gmeow:slices/organization): The closing time of an opening-hours window. Projects to schema:closes.

- gmeow:commitDescendant (property; gmeow:slices/software): The transitive closure of the inverse of parentCommit — any descendant commit in the DAG. Transitive, non-simple: kept out of all cardinality / functional axioms. Inverse of gmeow:commitAncestor.

- gmeow:derivationTarget (property; gmeow:slices/lexicon): The descendant lexical item or form that is derived from the source. Functional per relator: one target per EtymologicalDerivation.
- gmeow:derivationType (property; gmeow:slices/creative-works): The kind(s) of derivation relating source and product — cover, remix, sample, arrangement, etc. Non-functional: a single derivation may combine types (e.g. a sampled cover).
- gmeow:derivedFromSpectrum (property; gmeow:slices/music): Relates a PitchCollection to the Spectrum it was derived from. The actual derivation is performed by fnSpectrumToPitchCollection (Principle 12).
- gmeow:describesEvent (property; gmeow:slices/email): Links an email message to an event described within it — typically parsed from a text/calendar attachment. Non-functional: an email may describe multiple events, and an event may be described by multiple emails (updates, forwards, replies).
- gmeow:describesModel (property; gmeow:slices/ai): The model agent this card describes.
- gmeow:description (property; gmeow:slices/entities): A free-text note or description about an entity — the unstructured NOTE field (a biography, a remark, an annotation). Genuinely flat: unlike names, dates or roles, a note has no structure to reify. Distinct from skos:definition, which docu...
- gmeow:designGoal (property; gmeow:slices/languages): The stated design goal/purpose of an engineered or constructed language (Lojban's syntactic unambiguity, Ithkuil's cognitive precision, an IAL's ease of learning). A literal; non-functional.
- gmeow:detectedBy (property; gmeow:slices/ai): The agent (a person, an NLI model, an evaluation run's judge) that surfaced this contradiction. Attributed because detection is contestable. Not gmeow:vantage, which is domained on Observation — a Contradiction is a relator between claims,...
- gmeow:detectedMediaType (property; gmeow:slices/names): The MIME media type DETECTED from the bytes/magic of an information object (the observed type). May disagree with a filename's gmeow:claimedMediaType — a mismatch is recorded, not reasoned into a contradiction. Non-functional.
- gmeow:determinacyModel (property; gmeow:slices/places): Relates a reference frame to its default determinacy model.
- gmeow:developmentSignalEvent (property; gmeow:slices/narrative): A diegetic event the analyzer cited for this reading — an ordinary gmeow:Event claims-scoped accordingTo its narrative frame (existing doctrine), typically also narrated by the position's segment (#360). NOT functional.
- gmeow:developmentSignalText (property; gmeow:slices/narrative): Prose evidence the analyzer cited for this reading. NOT functional and range-open (localizable prose, the #376 convention).
- gmeow:diffFrom (property; gmeow:slices/software): The base commit of a diff — the 'before' state. Functional: a diff has exactly one base commit.
- gmeow:diffTo (property; gmeow:slices/software): The target commit of a diff — the 'after' state. Functional: a diff has exactly one target commit.
- gmeow:dimensionCount (property; gmeow:slices/places): The number of dimensions spanned by a reference frame.
- gmeow:discourseTimeOf (property; gmeow:slices/narrative): Anchors a discourse-time frame to the creative work (expression or manifestation tier) whose telling order it coordinatizes. Functional: one frame, one telling. Different editions or translations that re-segment the text own different disc...

- gmeow:dispositionNotificationTo (property; gmeow:slices/email): The email address to which a read receipt or other message disposition notification should be sent (RFC 3798 Disposition-Notification-To). Non-functional: multiple addresses may be listed.
- gmeow:distanceMetric (property; gmeow:slices/graphrag): The similarity/distance function under which an embedding or index is meaningful — cosine and euclidean disagree about what is 'near', so the metric is provenance, not a detail. Domain-free: carried by Embedding and VectorIndex alike.
- gmeow:distributionFormat (property; gmeow:slices/software): The format of a distribution artifact — e.g. 'tar.gz', 'wheel', 'docker-image', 'exe'.
- gmeow:dividedIntervalDenominator (property; gmeow:slices/music): The denominator of the interval that an equal-division tuning divides (e.g., 1 for the octave 2/1).
- gmeow:dividedIntervalNumerator (property; gmeow:slices/music): The numerator of the interval that an equal-division tuning divides (e.g., 2 for the octave 2/1; 3 for the Bohlen-Pierce tritave 3/1).
- gmeow:divisionCount (property; gmeow:slices/music): For equal-division tunings, the number of equal divisions of the period (e.g., 12 for 12-EDO, 19 for 19-EDO).
- gmeow:docsConcern (property; gmeow:slices/kernel): Links a term, slice, or documentation-bearing resource to a gmeow:DocumentationConcern. Used only by documentation projections; it carries no logical semantics and does not affect the OWL 2 DL core.

- gmeow:dofExpression (property; gmeow:slices/music): The Expression whose parameter determination this DegreeOfFreedom declares. Exactly one of dofWork or dofExpression is required per relator; SHACL enforces the XOR.

- gmeow:from (property; gmeow:slices/email): The author address of a message (RFC 5322 From).

- gmeow:geocodeFrame (property; gmeow:slices/places): The geocoding reference frame in which this code is expressed. Functional: a geocode is expressed in exactly one frame.
- gmeow:geocodeValue (property; gmeow:slices/places): The string value of a geocode in its reference frame — the canonical literal carrier. Per-system properties (plusCode, what3words, …) are convenience accessors; a single Geocode instance carries exactly one code value (enforced by SHACL).
- gmeow:geohash (property; gmeow:slices/places): A geohash string — a hierarchical spatial indexing system encoding latitude and longitude into a base32 string (e.g. 'u4pruydqqvj').
- gmeow:geometryDeterminacy (property; gmeow:slices/places): The ontic determinacy model of a geometry's boundary — crisp (surveyed), vague (approximate), fuzzy (probabilistic), or disputed. Non-functional: competing source classifications coexist.
- gmeow:geometryResult (property; gmeow:slices/places): The Geometry result of a coordinate observation — a point, line, or polygon expressed as WKT or GeoJSON. The reference frame is carried on the observation and propagates to the result via the existing property chain.
- gmeow:geometryType (property; gmeow:slices/places): The structural kind of a geometry (a gmeow:GeometryType individual). Non-functional: competing source classifications may differ (e.g. polygon vs multipolygon) and must coexist as evidence.
- gmeow:governanceModel (property; gmeow:slices/software): The governance model of a project — a value from the open gmeow:GovernanceModel vocabulary (BDFL, foundation, meritocracy, DAO, …). Non-functional: a project may transition models over time.

- gmeow:intervalAfter (property; gmeow:slices/temporal): Allen AFTER: this interval begins strictly after the related interval ends. Transitive inverse of gmeow:intervalBefore. (= time:intervalAfter)
- gmeow:intervalBefore (property; gmeow:slices/temporal): Allen BEFORE: this interval ends strictly before the related interval begins. Transitive. Inverse of gmeow:intervalAfter. (= time:intervalBefore)
- gmeow:intervalCoincidesWith (property; gmeow:slices/temporal): Allen EQUALS: this interval and the related interval share the same temporal extent. Symmetric and transitive. TEMPORAL simultaneity only, never identity of the intervals themselves. (= time:intervalEquals)
- gmeow:intervalContains (property; gmeow:slices/temporal): Allen CONTAINS: this interval's extent strictly contains the related interval's extent. Transitive inverse of gmeow:intervalDuring. (= time:intervalContains)
- gmeow:intervalDuring (property; gmeow:slices/temporal): Allen DURING: this interval's extent falls strictly within the related interval's extent. Transitive. Inverse of gmeow:intervalContains. (= time:intervalDuring)
- gmeow:intervalFinishedBy (property; gmeow:slices/temporal): Allen FINISHED-BY: inverse of gmeow:intervalFinishes. (= time:intervalFinishedBy)
- gmeow:intervalFinishes (property; gmeow:slices/temporal): Allen FINISHES: this interval and the related interval end together, and this one began later. NOT transitive. Inverse of gmeow:intervalFinishedBy. (= time:intervalFinishes)
- gmeow:intervalMeets (property; gmeow:slices/temporal): Allen MEETS: this interval ends exactly when the related interval begins. NOT transitive. Inverse of gmeow:intervalMetBy. (= time:intervalMeets)
- gmeow:intervalMetBy (property; gmeow:slices/temporal): Allen MET-BY: inverse of gmeow:intervalMeets. (= time:intervalMetBy)
- gmeow:intervalOverlappedBy (property; gmeow:slices/temporal): Allen OVERLAPPED-BY: inverse of gmeow:intervalOverlaps. (= time:intervalOverlappedBy)
- gmeow:intervalOverlaps (property; gmeow:slices/temporal): Allen OVERLAPS: this interval begins before and ends during the related interval. NOT transitive. Inverse of gmeow:intervalOverlappedBy. (= time:intervalOverlaps)
- gmeow:intervalStartedBy (property; gmeow:slices/temporal): Allen STARTED-BY: inverse of gmeow:intervalStarts. (= time:intervalStartedBy)
- gmeow:intervalStarts (property; gmeow:slices/temporal): Allen STARTS: this interval and the related interval begin together, and this one ends first. NOT transitive. Inverse of gmeow:intervalStartedBy. (= time:intervalStarts)

- gmeow:positionOrdinal (property; gmeow:slices/narrative): The ordinal coordinate of this position within its frame — a chapter index, scene number, or fabula sequence number. Functional within one position; ordering semantics belong to the frame, and comparisons to the solver layer (Principle 12).
- gmeow:postIn (property; gmeow:slices/organization): The organization a post belongs to. Functional — a post concerns exactly one organization.

- gmeow:postalAddressFrame (property; gmeow:slices/contacts): The postal/administrative reference frame in which this address is expressed. Functional: an address is expressed in exactly one frame. The default is gmeow:referenceFramePostalAddress.
- gmeow:postalCode (property; gmeow:slices/contacts): The postal/ZIP code coordinate value of a postal address, expressed along the gmeow:axisPostalCode axis of the postal reference frame.
- gmeow:postingAccount (property; gmeow:slices/finance): The ledger account this posting affects. Functional: a posting affects exactly one ledger account.
- gmeow:postingAmount (property; gmeow:slices/finance): The monetary amount of this posting, expressed as a MonetaryAmount with explicit currency frame. Functional: a posting has exactly one amount.

- gmeow:taskPriority (property; gmeow:slices/calendar): The priority of the task, 0-9, where 0 is undefined and 1 is highest. Aligned to iCalendar PRIORITY.
- gmeow:taskRecurrenceUntilDone (property; gmeow:slices/calendar): Whether this recurring task continues until marked done, rather than stopping at a fixed count or end date.
- gmeow:taskStatus (property; gmeow:slices/calendar): The status of the task — not-started, in-progress, completed, or cancelled.
- gmeow:telephone (property; gmeow:slices/contacts): A telephone number at which an agent can be reached.
- gmeow:tempoMapSegmentOf (property; gmeow:slices/music): The TempoMap that this segment belongs to. Functional per segment: one parent TempoMap.
- gmeow:tempoRatioApprox (property; gmeow:slices/music): A generated decimal approximation of an irrational tempo ratio, produced from tempoRatioExpression by the solver. A lossy projection, not the canonical value.
- gmeow:tempoRatioExpression (property; gmeow:slices/music): A canonical symbolic expression for an irrational tempo ratio (e.g. "sqrt(2)/2"), stored as a literal and never reasoner-parsed. The generated decimal approximation is tempoRatioApprox (Principle 4).
- gmeow:temporalCoverage (property; gmeow:slices/events): The temporal extent or scope of a creative work.
- gmeow:temporalPrecision (property; gmeow:slices/events): The granularity to which an event's time is known — a gmeow:TemporalPrecision value (day / month / year / decade / circa). Makes the determinacy of a date explicit instead of pretending every date is to-the-day.
- gmeow:tenureAgent (property; gmeow:slices/teleology): The agent whose intentional mode an intention-tenure records. Functional: one tenure, one agent.
- gmeow:tenureDeterminacy (property; gmeow:slices/places): The ontic determinacy model of this land tenure's boundary or claim — crisp (surveyed), vague (approximate), fuzzy (probabilistic), or disputed. Non-functional: sources may disagree on determinacy, and those claims coexist.
- gmeow:tenureIntention (property; gmeow:slices/teleology): The desire or intention the tenure records the agent as holding over its interval. Functional: one tenure, one mode. Commitment tenure is carried by the Commitment relator's own temporal scope (relators are time-indexed by construction); t...

- gmeow:tenurePlace (property; gmeow:slices/places): The place (parcel, lot, or spatial unit) over which the rights of this LandTenure apply. Functional: a tenure concerns exactly one place (constitutive of the situation's identity).
- gmeow:tenurePosition (property; gmeow:slices/standpoint): The standpoint-indexed claim the tenure says the standpoint held over its interval — a reified statement (a gmeow:StatementMetadata cell in the statement DSL). The range is intentionally left open: the statement-DSL spec layer is not part...
- gmeow:tenureRights (property; gmeow:slices/places): The machine-readable rights statement (permissions, prohibitions, duties) that governs this land tenure. Links to the #21 rights facility by reference. Non-functional: multiple legal instruments may apply to the same tenure (e.g. national...
- gmeow:tenureStandpoint (property; gmeow:slices/standpoint): The standpoint whose position a standpoint-tenure records. When a StandpointTenure generates a StandpointClaim observation, the tenureStandpoint becomes the vantage of the claim.
- gmeow:tenureType (property; gmeow:slices/places): The kind(s) of land tenure (a gmeow:LandTenureType individual). Non-functional: a single tenure may be classified by multiple sources as different types, and those claims coexist as evidence (Principle 9).
- gmeow:tenuredContactPoint (property; gmeow:slices/contacts): The contact point an address-tenure concerns.
- gmeow:textDirection (property; gmeow:slices/languages): The writing direction(s) of a writing system (gmeow:TextDirection values). Non-functional — Japanese is both vertical-rtl and ltr.
- gmeow:threadSubject (property; gmeow:slices/email): The base subject of a conversation thread, with reply/forward prefixes stripped, used for display and grouping. Derived from the raw RFC 5322 Subject headers of the messages in the thread.
- gmeow:timeDurationDenominator (property; gmeow:slices/music): The denominator of the rational duration of a MusicalTimeSpan in its frame. Always positive.
- gmeow:timeDurationNumerator (property; gmeow:slices/music): The numerator of the rational duration of a MusicalTimeSpan in its frame.
- gmeow:timeMappingKind (property; gmeow:slices/music): The kind of a TimeMapping (tuplet, tempo canon, metric modulation, groove, etc.). Functional: a TimeMapping is of exactly one kind.
- gmeow:timeStartDenominator (property; gmeow:slices/music): The denominator of the rational start position of a MusicalTimeSpan in its frame. Always positive.
- gmeow:timeStartNumerator (property; gmeow:slices/music): The numerator of the rational start position of a MusicalTimeSpan in its frame.
- gmeow:timeZoneIanaId (property; gmeow:slices/calendar): The IANA time zone identifier, e.g. America/Toronto, Europe/Paris, UTC.
- gmeow:timezone (property; gmeow:slices/places): An IANA time-zone identifier for a location (e.g. "America/Edmonton"). Non-functional: a large place may span several zones.
- gmeow:title (property; gmeow:slices/documents): The title of a creative work.
- gmeow:to (property; gmeow:slices/email): A primary recipient address of a message (RFC 5322 To).
- gmeow:toneEventArticulation (property; gmeow:slices/music): The articulation or attack quality applied to this ToneEvent.
- gmeow:toneEventDynamics (property; gmeow:slices/music): The symbolic dynamic level of this ToneEvent (ppp ... fff). Measured decibel observations use the observation layer, not this shortcut.
- gmeow:toneEventIsUnpitched (property; gmeow:slices/music): True when this ToneEvent has no definite pitch (e.g. percussion, noise). Mutually exclusive with toneEventPitchValue and toneEventPitchTrajectory.
- gmeow:toneEventPitchTrajectory (property; gmeow:slices/music): A continuous pitch trajectory sounded by this ToneEvent. Mutually exclusive with toneEventPitchValue and toneEventIsUnpitched.
- gmeow:toneEventPitchValue (property; gmeow:slices/music): A frame-relative pitch value sounded by this ToneEvent. Mutually exclusive with toneEventPitchTrajectory and toneEventIsUnpitched; SHACL enforces at most one pitch-content mode.
- gmeow:toneEventTimbre (property; gmeow:slices/music): A timbre descriptor applied to this ToneEvent; the full sensory bridge lands in M11 (#317).

- gmeow:trajectoryControlPoint (property; gmeow:slices/music): Relates a PitchTrajectory to one of its ordered control points. Non-functional: a trajectory has many control points.

- gmeow:trajectoryReferenceFrame (property; gmeow:slices/places): The coordinate reference frame in which this trajectory's samples are expressed. Functional: a trajectory is expressed in exactly one frame; frame transformation is a solver concern (Principle 12).
